site.tagline: C4FM (Yaesu System Fusion) digital voice on the Baofeng DM-32UV. An experimental fork of RadioFoundry.
home.title: C4FM on the DM-32UV
home.headline: C4FM digital voice on the Baofeng DM-32UV
home.lead: C4FMFoundry is an experimental fork of RadioFoundry that adds Yaesu System Fusion (C4FM DN voice) to the DM-32UV, beside FM and DMR, in one firmware. It uses the radio's own DMR chip and AMBE+2 codec: no hardware changes.
home.codec: The AMBE+2 codec is not on this site: the installer takes it from your own radio's firmware.
home.poc_text: It works on the air with Yaesu radios (callsign, DG-ID, voice both ways, repeaters and Wires-X), but the receiver is still weaker than a Yaesu radio's on weak signals. Use it to experiment, not as your only radio.
home.f_voice_text: Voice both ways in DN mode (V/D mode 2, AMBE+2 2450), direct and through Fusion repeaters.
home.f_id_text: Sends the callsign and a radio ID the way an FT-70D does; shows who is talking and keeps a Last heard list.
home.f_channels_text: C4FM is a channel mode in the codeplug, with its own DG-ID (0-99). Edit them in the Codeplug Editor on this site.
home.f_modes_text: FM, DMR voice, contacts and SMS work as in RadioFoundry. Left out to make room: IP and network services, the hotspot, APRS and the advanced DMR services.
home.f_wx_text: Node status, the room list, room search, connect and disconnect, from the radio (# on Home on a C4FM channel).
home.f_rx_text: A software demodulator on the radio's FM audio, with soft decision decoding of the headers and data channels.
home.how_1: Use Chrome or Edge on a desktop computer, with the radio's USB programming cable.
home.how_2: Open Install. The installer backs up your radio first: keep that file, it is your way back to the stock firmware.
home.how_3: It takes the AMBE+2 codec from your radio and writes the C4FM firmware with it.
home.how_4: Program C4FM channels with the Codeplug Editor, or set the DG-ID and callsign on the radio (Menu > C4FM).
home.not_1: GPS data (DT1/DT2), full rate voice (VW), pictures and text, and Fusion repeater link features.
home.not_2: Weak signal reception: Yaesu radios still hear further.
home.not_3: Other radios: this firmware is for the Baofeng DM-32UV only.
home.license: A mod by SQ5FOX, developed with Claude (Anthropic). RadioFoundry itself is developed with AI coding agents too: its repository ships notes for them (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md). Based on RadioFoundry (MIT); the C4FM layer is modeled on MMDVM, MMDVMHost, MMDVM_CM and YSFGateway (GPL-2.0). The C4FM code (core/c4fm) is GPL-2.0-or-later, so this firmware is a GPL-2.0-or-later work. Not affiliated with the RadioFoundry project or Yaesu. System Fusion and Wires-X are Yaesu trademarks.

flash.title: Install
flash.lead: Install the C4FM firmware on a Baofeng DM-32UV, back it up or restore it, over USB. Requires Chrome or Edge on a desktop computer.
flash.beta.title: This Is a Proof of Concept
flash.beta.lead: C4FMFoundry is an experiment by one radio amateur, built on RadioFoundry. It has been tested on one radio by hand, not by RadioFoundry's test bench. Read this before you start.
flash.beta.risk_features: C4FM reception is weaker than a Yaesu radio's, and some features of the original firmware are missing.
flash.beta.help_text: Something didn't work? Open an issue on GitHub with what happened. The Report a Problem button saves a file with the installer's log that you can attach. Please don't report problems with this firmware to the RadioFoundry project.
flash.log.summary: This installer sends nothing anywhere: no logs, no statistics, no error reports. The firmware image comes from this site; your radio's codec and backups stay on your computer.
editor.lead: Edit channels (FM, DMR and C4FM), zones, contacts and the DMR ID database, then write them to the radio or save them to a file. Everything stays on your computer.
